crop_file: # LEGEND (codes -> glyph shape, in words). This is one reader's best-effort shape vocabulary for an
# unfamiliar invented-symbol cipher alphabet, built while transcribing; it is NOT a claim about sound
# or letter values. Codes resembling Greek letters are named for visual resemblance only.
# [phi]   upward arrowhead/wedge sitting on a short stem, often a small ball or flag at the apex (commonest sign)
# [lam]   a plain peak/caret with no stem, like a narrow "^" (2nd commonest)
# [rho]   a small loop with a short descending tail, like a cursive "p" or rho
# [dag]   a small cross or dagger sitting on a short stem, a ball or crossbar at the top; recurs as its
#         own standalone token in the stream, not as a diacritic on a neighbour
# [f]     a small f-like glyph whose descender curls back to the left
# [z]     a z/7-shaped zigzag stroke (kept separate from the numeral-like [7], see below; the two may in
#         fact be the same sign inconsistently coded -- flagged for the reconciler)
# [n]     a double-hump stroke, like a Latin "n"
# [x]     a small plain x, thinner-stroked than [star]
# [7]     a numeral-7-like stroke (see note at [z] above)
# [ov]    two adjacent strokes read together as a single "o"+"v" ligature-like unit; may be an
#         over-merge of two separate signs -- flagged for the reconciler
# [theta] a circle with a horizontal bar through the middle
# [omg]   a wide double-hump letter, like omega or "w"
# [A]     a capital A, triangular with a crossbar
# [a]     a smaller a-like curl, kept distinct from [A] by size
# [star]  a bold asterisk/starburst with radiating strokes, distinct from [x]
# [psi]   a trident / three-tine fork on a stem (distinct from [phi]'s single wedge; the two are visually
#         close and may be confused in places -- flagged for the reconciler)
# [s]     a smaller s-curl, kept distinct from [S] by size
# [TO], [TA]  a T immediately followed by a small o or a-shaped loop, read as one unit in most places;
#         may be two adjacent signs (T + O/A) rather than one -- flagged for the reconciler

# [C6], [6]   a small closed loop like a 6 or G
